about: The text a value cell displays (ADR-0006, note of 2026-10-01; ADR-0350 section 16): empty for a Blank, the column's format where it has one, and otherwise the value's own text, a date in one ISO form by its type. From DisplayText and ColumnInfo.TextFor; the Script Core's cells/display-text.ts. A fractional number without a format is a double on both cores here, which reads as Excel's General does, in at most 15 significant digits (decided with the user, 2026-10-26). C#'s decimal keeps its trailing zeros and JavaScript's number cannot, so a decimal is left out; and so is a number of 1e17 or more, or below 0.0001, which C# writes with an exponent where JavaScript does not. The cases are read under the invariant culture.

cases.name: ADR-0006: a Blank shows nothing, with a format or without
ADR-0006: text shows itself, the empty string included
ADR-0350: a boolean reads True or False, as C#'s does, so a column reads alike on either core
ADR-0006: a whole number shows its digits
ADR-0350: a double reads as Excel's General, in at most 15 significant digits, so a binary fraction's last digits do not show
ADR-0006: a day reads yyyy-MM-dd, whatever the reader's culture
ADR-0006: a date and time reads yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss, its fraction of a second not shown
ADR-0006: an instant reads yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss with the offset it was written in
ADR-0350: a JavaScript Date holds no offset, and reads in UTC's
ADR-0006: a format decides the text of every value but a Blank
